text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful information; your recent improvement on risperidone suggests a positive response to treatment. Given your age, the specific medication started two months ago, and the new onset of movement issues, do you notice any stiffness, slowness, or involuntary muscle spasms in your limbs or face?

text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—specifically the inability to remain still, restlessness, and pacing—are classic signs of akathisia. Given your recent diagnosis of schizophrenia and the initiation of risperidone two months ago, this is a likely adverse effect of the medication. Have you noticed any worsening of these feelings after taking your dose, or do they persist throughout the day regardless of when you took your medication?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-induced Acute Akathisia. The clinical presentation of subjective restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to remain still in a patient recently started on risperidone is diagnostic for this side effect.
